To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
obesity related pathways are associated with inflammation, cellular stress, metabolic dysregulation, and immune dysregulation.
we performed pathway analysis on plasma proteomics data to identify pathways that are altered with obesity.

we performed pathway analysis on 3 independent plasma proteomic data sets from postmenopausal females and found that many pathways were consistently and significantly altered in plasma from obese subjects compared to plasma samples from normal BMI subjects and that these pathways are associated with inflammatory dysregulation, cellular stress, metabolic dysregulation, and immune dysregulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the pathways that are dysregualted during obesity and how these pathways are interconnected with each other and other diseases.

the development of novel methods for pathway analysis of large-scale data, the identification of pathways that are altered during obesity, and the description of interconnections between these pathways.
the use of proteomics and pathway analysis to understand the biological consequences of obesity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our results indicate that obesity is a systemic inflammatory condition and that the pathways dysregulated in obesity are similar to those activated during other diseases.

the proteomic and pathway analysis results presented in this thesis indicate that the inflammatory pathways are dysregulated in obese subjects and that these pathways are interconnected to other pathways that are dysreuglated in cancer and infection.
the proteome of plasma from obese subjects is altered compared to that of subjects with normal BMI and that these alterations are indicative of a dysregulated inflammatory state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

obesity is a risk modifier for other diseases and the mechanisms that underlie the risk modification are related to dysregulation of inflammation, metabolic dysregulation, and cellular stress pathways.
obesity alters pathways that are associated with inflammation, cell stress and metabolism.
obesity is a risk for disease because obesity dysregulates many pathways that also are dysregulated in cancer and infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
high-dimensional pathway analysis of proteomic data can provide a comprehensive understanding of biological processes altered in disease.

proteomic studies can offer a more holistic view of the biological implications of obesity and other diseases and that high-dimensional analysis can provide information on the interactions between pathways and help identify potential targets for treatment and intervention.
obesity is not a single pathway disease.
